title: Signs of a Take-Over
about: Spot when someone else is using your account.

cards.situation: 7:04 am. Your friend Jai has sent you a message.

image.alt: Your phone's lock screen at 7:04. A message from your friend Jai: Why did you send me this weird link?? Under it, a link: prize-win.example/free.

cards.prompt: Your Chat app keeps a list of what your account did. **Tap each line.**

parts.job: The app texts a code after your password is typed, to check it's you. You were signing in.
A laptop you don't own, while you were asleep. Someone else signed in with your password.
You, this morning, opening Jai's message.

cards.explanation: Three lines were you. One wasn't.

cards.prompt: Whoever got in still has your password. You do nothing. **What happens tonight?**

image.alt: Your Recent activity list: Laptop, 2:13 am, outlined; This phone, 7:04 am. Below, an empty dashed row for tonight. A moon and stars in the corner.
image.revealAlt: A new row at the bottom of the list: Laptop, tonight 1:48 am. Jai messages again: You sent it again?

options.text: They sign in again and send more links
The app throws them out on its own
They can't: a password only works once

cards.explanation: Your password still works for them, so they come back tonight.

cards.title: A take-over
cards.body: Someone else using your account is a **take-over**. The warning sign is anything your account did that **wasn't you**.

image.alt: The same activity list, each row tagged. Code sent 4:01 pm: You. This phone 4:02 pm: You. Laptop 2:13 am: Not you, with a warning sign. This phone 7:04 am: You.

cards.prompt: A new day. You only ever use your phone. **Tap the sign-in that wasn't you.**
cards.explanation: Right: you don't own a tablet, so that sign-in wasn't you.
cards.nudge: Look at the device on each line. Which one isn't yours?
cards.showAnswer: It's the tablet: you only use your phone, so someone else signed in.

cards.prompt: You're watching TV, not signing in. A Chat code pops up. **Tap what it means.**

image.alt: You're on the sofa watching TV in the evening. Your phone on the cushion shows a notification: Chat code: 482 913.
image.revealAlt: Your Recent activity list slides up. A new row: Code sent, today 7:30 pm, tagged Not you. No sign-in from you comes after it.

options.text: Warning sign: someone typed my password
Normal: apps send codes now and then
options.nudge: This morning, the 8:09 code came just before your own sign-in. Who's signing in now?

options.text: Normal: it's reminding me to sign in
options.nudge: This morning, the 8:09 code came just before your own sign-in. Who's signing in now?

cards.explanation: Yes: a code comes after someone types your password, and this time it wasn't you.
cards.showAnswer: It's a warning sign: someone else typed your password, because codes only come after that.

cards.prompt: Your own accounts this week. Some alerts are you, some aren't. **Sort each one.**

items.label: Sign-in alert as you set up a new phone
Friends got a link you never sent
A post on your page you didn't make
Asked to sign in again after an update

cards.explanation: Anything that wasn't you is a warning sign; an alert that matches what you just did is you.
cards.nudge: For each one, ask: did I just do this, or did someone else?
cards.showAnswer: The link and the post weren't you, so they're warning signs. The other two match something you did.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
Anything your account did that **wasn't you** is a warning sign. Spot one? Tell a trusted adult.

**Try this:** Open one app's settings and find the list of devices signed in to your account.

**Next:** How to kick whoever got in out of your account, and keep them out.
